experiments.claim: Reflection, conjugation and strict positivity on the critical line do not imply RH for general entire functions.
assumptions: The explicitly defined degree-four polynomial is not the completed zeta function.
falsifiers: Evaluate the four purported roots with exact Gaussian rational arithmetic.
Check the global sum-of-squares lower bound on the critical line.
limitations: This blocks an invalid inference; it does not establish any statement about zeros of zeta.

experiments.claim: The S9/S10 Lean-ready algebraic identities (cos/cosh at Fourier nodes, Re(t+iθ)^{-2}, sign-lemma factorization, 2x2 Gram energy, and the untempered |a(p)| rewrite) hold exactly.
assumptions: Sympy's exact simplification is a faithful check of the named elementary identities.
falsifiers: Any identity whose simplified residual is nonzero fails the script's asserts.
limitations: These are algebraic identities used in later numerical work; they do not imply RH.
Requires sympy (see requirements.txt). Not part of the stdlib smoke set.

experiments.claim: The Davenport–Heilbronn coefficient κ equals √(φ+2)−φ = 5^{1/4}√φ−φ, and ε(χ)=(φ+i)/√(φ+2), with 400-bit Arb balls containing the residuals.
assumptions: The conductor-5 odd character and the classical DH functional equation are as in the script docstring.
python-flint Arb at 400 bits is a correct interval implementation.
falsifiers: Any named residual ball that does not contain 0.
limitations: φ is forced by the choice q=5, not by RH.
Requires python-flint. Not part of the stdlib smoke set.

experiments.claim: High-precision floating-point checks of P(λ)=πλ/sinh(πλ): Fourier pair against sech²(x/2)/4, Planck representation at β=2π, logarithmic derivative, and Matsubara residues.
assumptions: mpmath quadrature and differentiation at 60 decimal places bound the residuals below the script's stated tolerances.
falsifiers: Any relative residual exceeding the script's asserts (1e-40 / 1e-45 / 1e-15).
limitations: NUMERICAL (float, mpmath). Not an interval certificate and not a statement about RH.
Requires mpmath. Not part of the stdlib smoke set.

experiments.claim: Float checks that the Kubo–Mori kernel at β=2π matches P(λ), and that the archimedean Weil term matches a Lévy–Khintchine representation with jump density ν(u)=2e^{-u/2}/(1-e^{-2u}).
assumptions: mpmath at 30 decimal places, with the script's quadrature splits, is accurate enough to read residuals.
falsifiers: A large residual between the digamma difference and the Lévy integral, or between the Kubo–Mori kernel and P(λ).
limitations: Requires mpmath. Not part of the stdlib smoke set.

experiments.claim: The pole-renormalized prime jump measure M_prime((0,R]) = 2 Σ_{n≤e^R} Λ(n)/√n tracks 4(e^{R/2}−1) at the sampled R, and the DH logarithmic-derivative coefficients b(n) are neither nonnegative nor supported only on prime powers.
assumptions: Ordinary floating-point sums of von Mangoldt weights up to e^{14} suffice to see the sign of the difference.
falsifiers: Nonnegative, prime-power-supported b(n) for the conductor-5 DH combination up to n=60 would refute part (B).
limitations: NUMERICAL (float). Not certified and not a statement about RH.
Requires mpmath. Not part of the stdlib smoke set.
